rules.rule: Every fact is correct; an unconfirmed fact is left out
rules.how: Check each hard-to-remember fact against a source

rules.rule: Every worked answer, example answer, and key is correct
rules.how: Solve it yourself from the question alone
rules.source: LSG: Examples section; QSG: Blind solve

rules.rule: Required content is present: outline sections, required figures
rules.how: Compare with the outline entry and figure needs

rules.rule: Each checked fact has a source ledger entry, in a ledger that states its branch, base commit, and access date
rules.how: Find the item id in the round's ledger

rules.rule: The higher source wins, the conflict is recorded, and weak sources are never used alone
rules.how: Compare the cited source with the hierarchy

rules.rule: No em dashes
rules.how: Search for the character

rules.rule: American spelling in English text
rules.how: Look for British forms such as "colour", "practise"

rules.rule: Maths notation: `\dfrac` at top level, numbers in prose inside `$...$`, no `\( \)` or `\[ \]`
rules.how: Search the text
rules.source: LSG: Math notation; `AGENTS.md`: Maths in content

rules.rule: "points" not "marks", "questions" not "cards"
rules.how: Search the text

rules.rule: No FSRS, stability, retention, retrievability, or algorithm in student text
rules.how: Search the text

rules.rule: A learning goal is recorded and the lesson serves it
rules.how: Find the goal in the audit records; compare with the content

rules.rule: Teaching prose is very simple English a Grade 5 student can read, with no filler
rules.how: Read as a Grade 5 student; flag long or rare-word sentences

rules.rule: Exam instruction words with an exam-specific meaning are explained in one line on first use; everyday words are not
rules.how: Find the first use of each exam verb

rules.rule: At most one analogy, in Core Concept
rules.how: Count analogies

rules.rule: Example questions use exam wording and supply necessary problem-specific givens without supplying tested knowledge; solutions use simple language
rules.how: Check example stems against the expected-knowledge rule and compare wording with solutions

rules.rule: In-lesson quiz items meet every Q rule
rules.how: Run the question checks

rules.rule: Mentions of exams vary and motivate
rules.how: Look for repeated openers

rules.rule: Filipino lessons teach in simple Filipino at the Grade 5 standard
rules.how: Read as a Grade 5 student

rules.rule: A hard Filipino grammar term gets a short English gloss on first use only
rules.how: Find first uses

rules.rule: Filipino lessons' examples and quiz items are in Filipino
rules.how: Check each example and item

rules.rule: Filipino spelling and usage follow the Komisyon sa Wikang Filipino
rules.how: Check contested forms against the source

rules.rule: No Taglish in Filipino teaching prose
rules.how: Flag English words that are not the common term

rules.rule: No ALL-CAPS emphasis; bold for first definitions; italics rare
rules.how: Scan for capitals and emphasis

rules.rule: Target words are bold and the prompt says "the word in bold"
rules.how: Check prompts that refer to a word

rules.rule: No stock AI phrasing; varied sentence openings; a plainly varied summary
rules.how: Search for the listed phrases; read openings

rules.rule: Section titles are exact; mnemonics only when genuine; extra sections sparing
rules.how: Compare headings with the guide

rules.rule: Subject section fit is followed; every formula appears in Core Concept before any example uses it
rules.how: Trace each formula in examples back to Core Concept

rules.rule: Examples cover every distinct exam-relevant scenario, variation, and edge case within the learning goal, ramp from basic to target-exam difficulty, and avoid near-duplicates
rules.how: Map each distinct case to a worked example; check the difficulty progression and repeated reasoning

rules.rule: Solutions with two or more steps show every step as a numbered list, key computations as display equations
rules.severity: Major if a step is skipped, otherwise Minor
rules.how: Follow each solution step by step

rules.rule: Example and trap headings use `### #N: Title`; traps have a one-line warning and a short explanation
rules.how: Compare with the format

rules.rule: Display equations fit a phone screen
rules.how: Look for long display lines

rules.rule: Only allowed formatting: no tables, links, code blocks, or horizontal rules
rules.how: Search for the banned syntax

rules.rule: Paragraphs are one to three short sentences; bullet lists are sparing
rules.how: Scan paragraphs

rules.rule: Each placeholder is one specific line an artist could draw from; the prose teaches without the image except where the figure is the question (missing required figures fall under B03)
rules.how: Read each placeholder

rules.rule: Frontmatter has the exact shape and outline slugs
rules.how: Compare with the template and the outline

rules.rule: Necessary terms, symbols, and units are explained before their meanings are needed
rules.how: Trace needed meanings to local teaching, an identified prerequisite, or a clearly signposted later section under the shared reuse rule

rules.rule: Concepts explain their meaning and how they work, not just names or formulas
rules.how: Find the explanation under the shared reuse rule; confirm that the current learning goal is taught

rules.rule: Relevant conditions, limitations, and exceptions explain when a rule, formula, or shortcut applies
rules.how: Check applicability explanations under the shared reuse rule
